companyIntro.name: Atlas Manufacturing
companyIntro.mission: World-class manufacturing discipline — every defect has a root cause, and every root cause gets fixed once, not patched repeatedly.
companyIntro.culture: Lean-first and data-driven. Line staff and engineers alike are expected to know their process' current defect rate from memory.

projectBackground.name: Line 3 Performance Recovery
projectBackground.context: Line 3 misses its weekly output. Management wants to know where the lost capacity actually goes.

manager.name: Min-jun Park
manager.note: Don't tell me the line is slow; tell me which losses are costing us units and which we can fix first.

assignment.title: Find and recover the lost capacity
assignment.brief: Calculate OEE, utilisation and takt, identify the bottleneck and write a shift plan.

documents.name: Shift Schedule
documents.note: 450 productive minutes per day; daily demand 225 units.

tasks.title: OEE
tasks.prompt: Availability 90%, performance 95%, quality 98%. What is OEE (%)?
tasks.reasoning: OEE multiplies the three loss categories.
tasks.tip: Report each factor, not just OEE.
tasks.mistake: Averaging the factors gives 94.3%, which is wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Capacity Utilisation
tasks.prompt: Weekly demand is 4,800 units and capacity is 6,000. What is utilisation (%)?
tasks.mistake: Running at 100% leaves no room for variation.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Takt Time
tasks.prompt: 450 productive minutes per day and 225 units of daily demand. What is takt time in minutes per unit?
tasks.reasoning: Takt is the pace needed to meet demand.
tasks.tip: Compare takt to cycle time per station.
tasks.mistake: Using total shift time including breaks understates takt.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Bottleneck
tasks.prompt: Where should improvement effort go first?
options: At the bottleneck station that limits the whole line
tasks.reasoning: Output is limited by the constraint; improving elsewhere changes nothing.
tasks.mistake: Improving non-bottlenecks creates inventory, not output.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Reducing Downtime
tasks.prompt: Select actions that reduce availability losses.
tasks.reasoning: Understanding and attacking stops raises availability.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring small stops hides cumulative loss.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Shift Plan
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence plan for the next shift to recover capacity.
tasks.modelAnswer: Next shift we focus on the packing station, the constraint, with a 2 minute takt target. We will standardise the changeover with a checklist and record every stop over two minutes by reason. Preventive maintenance on the packing sealer moves to the start of the shift. Output, OEE and top three stop reasons will be reviewed at the end of shift.
tasks.reasoning: A good plan targets the constraint, names actions and measures results.
tasks.mistake: Spreading effort thinly across the line yields no gain.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Fast Machine
caseStudy.background: A plant bought a faster filling machine, but output didn't change. Packing, the true bottleneck, couldn't keep up and inventory built up.
caseStudy.solution: Atlas required a constraint study before any capital request.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Improve the constraint, not the convenient.
